newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures settled higher in thin volume with the market in a wait-and-see mood ahead of the outcome of a meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee.
Some dealers said the possibility of a 25-basis point hike in the Fed funds rate was already priced into the market but others said that it could react badly to an increase.

Others were betting the Fed would leave rates unchanged. "There's growth in the United States but no pressure on prices. A rise would not be justified today. (Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan) Greenspan has time to wait," said an analyst.

The 10-year bond future spent the day fluctuating in a narrow 20-point range between 128.06 and 128.26 before settling up 24 basis points at 128.10. June PIBOR gained two points to 96.54. The franc strengthened slightly against the mark to 3.3722/27 compared with 3.3731/37 on Thursday.
One analyst said if the Fed does tighten, the 10-year bond future could fall to 127.74. If it leaves rates unchanged, it could rise to 129.00.
But if the Fed holds steady, "we could soon go back to having the markets nervous and on the defensive" in expectation of a hike, one analyst said.
